entities.name: Victor of Vita
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Victor Vitensis was an African bishop of the Province of Byzacena, whose Historia persecutionis Africanae Provinciae, written during the reigns of Genserici and Hunirici, king of the Vandals, remains a valuable source for understanding the persecutions faced by African Christians during the 5th century CE.

As bishop of Byzacena, Victor Vitensis played a crucial role in the administration of the province, overseeing the governance of its cities and clergy.

The Historia persecutionis Africanae Provinciae, which chronicles the persecution of African Christians during the reigns of Genserici and Hunirici, is considered a significant work in the history of Christian persecution.

Victor Vitensis's legacy can be seen in the enduring impact of his work on Christian historiography and the ongoing study of the persecution of African Christians during the 5th century CE.

A striking statistic is that the Historia persecutionis Africanae Provinciae has been translated into several languages, including Latin, Greek, and Arabic, and remains an important source for historians and scholars today.
